advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make mcp_retire_sweep refuse to retire anything (or abort with a marker) when mcp_live_port yields no live port, so an unreadable upstream include cannot cause the sweep to stop the live backend.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:405: `live="$(mcp_live_port)"`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:409: `[ -n "$live" ] && [ "$p" = "$live" ] && continue   # keep the live backend (RELEASES_KEEP)`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:310: `mcp_live_port() { sed -nE '...' "$MCP_UPSTREAM_FILE" 2>/dev/null | head -1; }` — echoes nothing when the file is absent/empty/unparseable
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:465: `mcp_retire_sweep          # reap mcp containers that finished draining since the last flip` runs on the no-op tick

ABSENCE: every test in test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py seeds a populated upstream (e.g. line 229 `upstream.write_text("server 127.0.0.1:8091;\n")`); no test exercises an empty/missing MCP_UPSTREAM_FILE, so this case is uncovered.
advisory.finding: mcp_retire_sweep retires the LIVE backend when mcp_live_port returns empty. The keep-guard `[ -n "$live" ] && [ "$p" = "$live" ] && continue` is short-circuited to false for every container whenever `live` is empty (MCP_UPSTREAM_FILE missing, empty, or not matching the `server 127.0.0.1:<port>;` pattern), so every managed mcp container — including the one currently serving /mcp — is graceful-stopped. Because the sweep runs on every up-to-date/no-op tick, a missing or malformed upstream include would silently take the MCP endpoint down.
advisory.suggested_fix: When `live` is empty, treat the live port as unknown and skip retiring entirely (return early after emitting a diagnostic marker), rather than falling through and stopping every managed container.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit a distinct countable marker when the memory reading is unreadable (mcp_mem == -1) so a fail-open memory guard is observable rather than silent.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:632: `if [ "$mcp_mem" -ge 0 ] && [ "$mcp_mem" -lt "$MCP_MEM_MIN_MB" ]; then`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:314-322: mcp_mem_available_mb echoes -1 for unreadable, and -1 fails the `-ge 0` test so the abort branch is skipped with no marker

infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:133: comment 'Unreadable fails OPEN (a broken probe must not wedge deploys)' — documented intent, but no countable signal distinguishes 'checked and clear' from 'probe never produced a reading'
advisory.finding: The low-memory abort emits AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT, but the fail-open branch (unreadable MemAvailable → mcp_mem_available_mb returns -1) proceeds with the 2x-overlap deploy while emitting no distinct signal that the memory guard did not actually run. A chronically broken /proc/meminfo read is therefore indistinguishable from a box that is genuinely above the floor.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an `elif [ "$mcp_mem" -lt 0 ]` branch that emits a diagnostic marker (kept out of deploy_errors) before proceeding, so 'probe unreadable' is distinguishable from 'memory OK'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the `--restart always` policy on blue-green mcp containers with the docker-stop retire model (use `--restart unless-stopped`, or `docker rm` the retired container once drained, so a reboot does not resurrect stale/old-port containers).
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:347-349 `docker run -d --name "$1" \` / `--restart always \`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:396 `( docker stop --time "$MCP_STOP_GRACE" "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) &` — retire is a stop, not a rm, for still-draining containers
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:412-413 exited containers are only reaped on a later tick via `docker rm`; between stop and reap a reboot can re-launch them
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:382-383 `logging:` / `driver: journald`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:347-367 `mcp_run_new` sets `--restart`, `--stop-timeout`, `--env-file`, `-e`, `-p`, `-v` but no `--log-driver`
infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:190-214 root-disk ENOSPC incident 2731 rationale (30G root, docker storage)
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:347-367 `mcp_run_new` has no `--network` flag
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml has no explicit `networks:` (search returned no matches), so compose uses the auto-created project default network
ABSENCE: no evidence the mcp service needs to reach other compose services on the shared network (reached by nginx via 127.0.0.1 published port)
advisory.finding: Blue-green mcp containers are started with `--restart always`, but retirement only issues `docker stop` (leaving exited-but-unreaped containers). Docker restarts `always`-policy containers on daemon/host reboot even if manually stopped, so a retired old-release container will be resurrected on reboot, re-binding its stale blue/green host port (8092/8093) and serving a stale image — colliding with or shadowing the live backend.
merged_from: `mcp_run_new` does not set `--log-driver journald`, so the blue-green containers diverge from the compose `mcp:` service (`logging: driver: journald`) and default to the json-file driver, writing unbounded container logs to the 30G root disk that previously hit ENOSPC (incident 2731). The compose-parity test only asserts env/volumes/restart/stop-timeout, not the logging driver, so this drift is uncaught.

The blue-green `docker run` does not attach the new mcp container to the compose project network (no `--network`), so it lands on the default bridge rather than the compose default network the boot-time `compose-mcp-1` uses. This is likely acceptable (mcp is reached only by host nginx over a published loopback port and appears not to call sibling services), but it is an undocumented divergence from the compose service topology not covered by the parity test.
scenarios: Host/daemon reboot while one or more retired mcp containers are stopped-but-not-yet-reaped
EC2 instance restart after a maintenance window
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `--restart unless-stopped` for the transient blue-green containers (so a manual `docker stop` survives reboot) and/or have the retire path `docker rm` the container once drained rather than leaving stopped containers with an `always` policy.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the gerrit blast-radius assertion fatal (record_backoff_failure + exit 1) rather than a bare log, so a detected blast-radius violation actually halts the deploy.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh (mcp block) `if [ -n "$gerrit_before_mcp" ] && [ "$gerrit_before_mcp" != "$gerrit_after_mcp" ]; then` / `err blast-radius "gerrit container id changed during an mcp deploy — investigate"` with no exit
comment claims 'The gerrit container is never touched (blast-radius assert)' at autodeploy.sh:611-612 but the assert is non-fatal
advisory.finding: The gerrit blast-radius assertion only emits an `err` marker when the gerrit container id changes during an mcp deploy; it does not `record_backoff_failure`/`exit 1` or roll back. The deploy proceeds to prune and reports success, so a genuine blast-radius violation is detected but not contained.
scenarios: A future change or a shared docker-compose path accidentally recreates gerrit during the mcp deploy

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat a failed `docker tag` of the immutable mcp release as fatal (err + record_backoff_failure + exit 1) instead of `|| true`.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh `docker tag "$MCP_IMAGE" "$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:367 `"$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` is the image `mcp_run_new` runs
advisory.finding: `docker tag "$MCP_IMAGE" "$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` swallows a tag failure. If tagging fails, `mcp_run_new` later references `"$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"`, which is missing, and the failure surfaces as an opaque `mcp-run-failed` instead of a clear tag error.
scenarios: The build succeeds but the SHA tag step fails (e.g. transient daemon error)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a producer-liveness anchor to test_unreadable_memory_fails_open (assert `run --name` is present or result.returncode == 0) so the absence of the mem-abort marker proves fail-open rather than an early exit.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:393-399: `result = _run(mcp_box, {"MCP_MEM_AVAILABLE_MB": "", "MCP_MEM_MIN_MB": "1024"}) ... assert not _markers(result, "AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT")`
cmds is bound via `_commands_eventually(mcp_box, "run --name")` at line 394 but no assertion consumes it
Fail-open contract in source (autodeploy.sh:630-635): the deploy proceeds past the memory check; the test does not assert that proceeding happened

Absence-only oracle: worlds where AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT is absent include 'deploy failed before the memory check' and 'mcp block never entered', which the test cannot distinguish from the intended fail-open
advisory.finding: test_unreadable_memory_fails_open is a fail-open oracle: it asserts ONLY the absence of the AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT marker with no liveness anchor proving the deploy actually reached and passed the memory gate. The 'fail-open' contract requires the deploy to PROCEED (start a container / succeed) when the memory reading is unreadable, but the test never asserts a container was run or that the run exited 0. The marker is trivially absent whenever the deploy fails early for any unrelated reason or never enters the mcp block, so the passing verdict is indistinguishable from the fail-open path being broken. The computed `cmds = _commands_eventually(mcp_box, "run --name")` is never asserted.
advisory.suggested_fix: After asserting no AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT marker, add `assert any(c.startswith("run --name") for c in cmds), ctx` (or assert the deploy reached the flip/succeeded) so the absence check is anchored to the deploy actually proceeding past the memory gate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an anti-vacuity floor to test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service asserting the compose parser extracted the expected env keys and both secret-mount volumes before the parity loops run.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:641-652: `for key, value in env.items(): assert f"-e {key}={value}" in run_line ...` and `for vol in volumes: ...` — no assertion that env/volumes are non-empty
_parse_compose_mcp_env_and_volumes returns dicts populated only when `re.match(r"^      ([A-Z0-9_]+):\s*(.+?)\s*$", ln)` matches (line 617), coupling correctness to the exact 6-space YAML indent
Contrast in same changeset — test_alarm_actions_terraform.py:38 `_MIN_EXPECTED_ALARMS = 15` and test_parser_actually_finds_the_alarms guard vacuity explicitly; the compose parser has no equivalent
advisory.finding: The compose-parity test derives its expected env/volumes by regex-parsing docker-compose.yml and then asserts inside `for key, value in env.items()` / `for vol in volumes` loops, with NO anti-vacuity floor asserting env and volumes are non-empty. If a docker-compose.yml reformat (indentation change, tabs, or an `environment:` list form) makes the parser match zero keys, both loops iterate zero times and the parity oracle passes silently — allowing exactly the env/mount drift the test exists to catch. This is notable because the sibling test in the same changeset (test_alarm_actions_terraform.py) explicitly guards this failure mode with _MIN_EXPECTED_ALARMS.
advisory.suggested_fix: After `env, volumes = _parse_compose_mcp_env_and_volumes()`, assert a minimum e.g. `assert len(env) >= 12 and len(volumes) == 2, "compose mcp parser matched too little — parity oracle would pass vacuously"` (or assert specific required keys like REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ENABLED are present).

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that feeds a real emitted AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP / AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT marker line through observability.sh's record-anchored grep pattern and asserts a non-zero delta is published.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:339-341: `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta '^AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP \{' mcp_retire_cap ...` and `'^AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT \{' mcp_mem_abort`
Producer format autodeploy.sh:206: `marker() { printf '%s %s\n' "$1" "$(python3 -c ...)" ...` — token, space, JSON object
search of tests/ for `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` returns (no matches); the marker-delta consumer path is untested for the new tokens
The bluegreen tests assert the marker is EMITTED (test file lines 379/428) but nothing asserts observability.sh's grep anchor matches that emitted line
blocking.finding: The new observability.sh marker-delta publishers for mcp_retire_cap / mcp_mem_abort — including their record-anchored ERE grep patterns '^AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP \{' and '^AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT \{' — have no test. autodeploy's marker() emits the token followed by a SPACE then '{' (autodeploy.sh:206 `printf '%s %s\n'`), and the alarm pipeline depends on the observability grep anchor matching that exact producer format; nothing exercises the coupling. A drift on either side (marker format change, or a mismatched anchor) would silently break the CloudWatch counter with no failing test.
